acts.text: In this walkthrough, we take a realistic Jenkins pipeline for inventory service—complete with parallel stages, a matrix, and a manual deployment gate—and prove its GitHub Actions conversion behaves identically.

First, j-two-g-h-a analyzes the pipeline using Jenkins' own Groovy parser into a typed intermediate model. It then converts it deterministically, handing the workspace between jobs, and validates with actionlint and zizmor.

Next, differential trace mode executes both [pipelines](/pˈIplˈInz/) side by side. It compares control flow across forty-one trace events, confirming a one hundred percent behavioural match without guessing.

Finally, the workflow runs on real GitHub Actions using disposable self-hosted runners, and every job passes with the same trace as Jenkins. From Jenkins to GitHub Actions—fully verified with evidence.
